== Biography ==

The White Rabbit is a figure of authority in Wonderland's court, bearing a trumpet and a scroll of parchment. During the trial of the Knave of Hearts, he maintains order and decorum, calling out "Silence in the court!" when others speak out of turn. His manner toward the King is fastidiously respectful, though he does not hesitate to correct what he perceives as the monarch's errors—once interrupting to say "Unimportant, your Majesty means, of course" in a dutiful tone, even as he frowned and made faces in contradiction.

The White Rabbit carries himself with considerable consequence and concern for propriety. He dresses splendidly, with white kid gloves and a large fan always in hand. He maintains a household marked with his initials—"W. RABBIT"—engraved upon a bright brass plate, and appears to command servants who run his errands, fetching his gloves and fan at his word. His attention is much occupied with the Duchess, whose favor he anxiously seeks, muttering to himself in worry lest he has kept her waiting.

== Relationships ==

'''[[Alice]]''' — acquaintance. The Rabbit reacts with alarm to Alice's approach, dropping his gloves and fan in a startled fashion.

'''[[King]]''' — appears to serve as a court official. The Rabbit maintains courtroom order, presents evidence at the sovereign's direction, and demonstrates careful deference to royal authority, though he permits himself gentle corrections of the King's language.

'''[[Duchess]]''' — seems to work in service to the Duchess. The Rabbit's anxious concern for his mistress dominates his attention, and he greatly fears her displeasure.

'''[[Mary Ann]]''' — appears to command household servants. The Rabbit gives urgent orders to Mary Ann to fetch his gloves and fan, suggesting he holds authority over domestic staff.
